skill.name: form-cro
skill.description: Optimize lead, contact, demo, application, survey, quote, checkout, and other non-signup forms for higher completion and lower friction.
skill.summary: Audit non-signup forms with a 100-point friction index and prioritized conversion fixes.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives in UX guidance text. The references are not executable code and show no keylogging, reconnaissance, exfiltration, or prompt injection intent.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line says validation should happen after field interaction, not per keystroke. It discourages keystroke-level behavior and contains no code, logging, or data collection instructions.
The line warns against using placeholder text as a label in a form. This is UX guidance, not system reconnaissance or environment inspection.
The line is a bad example of an error message for a form field. It contains no system probing, command use, or data access instruction.
The line is a sample user-facing validation message showing an email format. It does not instruct collection, storage, or transmission of sensitive data beyond normal form copy.

content.value_statement: Teams lose form submissions when fields, copy, and errors create avoidable friction. This skill audits non-signup forms and turns findings into prioritized fixes and tests.
actual_capabilities: Calculates a Form Health and Friction Index with weighted categories.
Reviews field necessity, value-effort balance, cognitive load, trust, and mobile usability.
Recommends required and optional fields with clear justification.
Suggests labels, help text, CTA copy, error messages, and layout notes.
Generates A/B test hypotheses and measurement guidance.
limitations: Does not cover signup or account registration forms.
Requires form context, goals, and analytics for precise recommendations.
Does not replace legal, compliance, or accessibility review.
Provides guidance only; teams must implement and test changes.

use_cases.title: Improve Demo Requests
use_cases.description: Audit a demo request form, reduce unnecessary friction, and improve qualified submission rates.

use_cases.title: Redesign Application Forms
use_cases.description: Prioritize required fields, clarify copy, and structure longer forms into useful steps.

use_cases.title: Audit Mobile Usability
use_cases.description: Check touch targets, keyboard behavior, autofill support, and layout issues on mobile forms.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Form Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit for a known form.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this contact form for completion friction. Include a Form Health and Friction Index, top bottlenecks, and three priority fixes: [form details].

prompt_templates.title: Field Justification Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of required and optional fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these form fields and decide which should be required, optional, removed, or moved later. Explain the business reason for each change.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Step Form Redesign
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this long form into a multi-step flow. Include step order, progress behavior, saved input handling, CTA copy, and error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Experiment Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing plan for a conversion team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized A/B testing roadmap for this form. Include hypotheses, expected outcomes, primary metrics, guardrail metrics, and experiment boundaries.

output_examples.input: A nine-field demo request form has low mobile completion.
output_examples.output: The audit identifies high effort, weak value copy, and mobile layout friction. It recommends fewer required fields, clearer CTA copy, and field-level tracking.

output_examples.input: A quote form uses generic errors and many required fields.
output_examples.output: The output rewrites error messages, separates optional fields, and proposes a test for a shorter first step.

output_examples.input: A survey form has no field-level analytics.
output_examples.output: The response lists measurement gaps, tracking events, and questions needed before a confident redesign.

best_practices: Start with the friction index before recommending changes.
Keep required fields tied to legal, routing, or immediate follow-up needs.
Validate after interaction and preserve entered data on errors.
anti_patterns: Removing fields without checking whether sales or operations use them.
Testing several form changes in one experiment.

faq.question: What forms does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports lead, contact, demo, application, survey, quote, checkout, and other non-signup forms.

faq.question: Does it optimize account registration?
faq.answer: No. Signup and account registration flows are outside this skill scope.

faq.question: What inputs improve the audit?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include current fields, business goals, completion rate, field drop-off, device split, and compliance constraints.

faq.question: Can it write final production copy?
faq.answer: It can draft labels, help text, CTA copy, and error messages for review and testing.

faq.question: Does it provide analytics guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends tracking form starts, completions, errors, submit attempts, field drop-off, and time to complete.

faq.question: How should teams use the recommendations?
faq.answer: Start with high-priority structural fixes, then test tactical changes with clear metrics and guardrails.
